newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: NetCare in healthy JSE debut.
newsitem.headline: NetCare in healthy JSE debut.

text.p: Shares in NetCare Ltd, a specialist hospital management company, made a healthy debut on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE) on Wednesday starting out 30 percent above its issue price in brisk dealings.
Dealers said the share had attracted a lot of stags -- players who apply for new securities on the chance of selling it for a profit -- who were oiling the market with stock.
"There are a lot of stags in the market. With no public offer some people took stock in the private and preferential offers to try make a profit at the listing," one trader said.

Network Healthcare Holdings Ltd's (NetCare) first trade was at 130 cents, its highest level so far, from an issue price of 100 cents. By 0825 GMT it had slid back to 124 cents after 1.8 million shares worth over 2.3 million rand changed hands.
Dealers said the share was seen capped around the 124-126 cent level on Wednesday with a wider 116-130 cent range seen in the short term.
NetCare combines the businesses of former specialist medical corporation Clin-Run as well as several of Clin-Run's managed hospitals and clinics.
Ahead of the listing shares were placed by way of a preferential offer of 65 million shares and a private placing of 60 million shares. The offers were fully subscribed.
In its prelisting statement NetCare forecast after-tax profit in the year to end-August 1997 of more than 23.6 million rand on turnover of 172 million rand.

At a presentation last month, Netcare managing director and founder Jack Shevel said that by listing it hoped to offset its debts and expand into South Africa's rapidly changing managed healthcare industry.
